name: pdk-linref-dataframe
instr:
Our road inventory now includes point survey observations as well as road ranges. Calling `linref.integrate` in `/app` on their LRS configured pandas frames with `split_at_locs=True` should return the least common road intervals, with an inverse column for each input. A sample is in `/data/survey/road-ranges.csv` and `/data/survey/observations.csv`. Right now the observations disappear from the inverse columns even when the intervals split.

The first input is a linear road frame. A point at an interval's beginning belongs to that interval, not the one before it. Points beyond road coverage do not extend the output; with `fill_gaps=False`, intervals with no road range are omitted. With `expand=False`, choose the first matching row in source order from each input; with `expand=True`, retain every combination of overlapping ranges and observations, including separate observations at the same site. An unmatched input gets a missing inverse value. Keep original index labels without converting numeric or text labels, and retain the caller's inverse column names. An empty observation frame should behave like one with no matches. Repeated calls on unchanged frames should return the same rows. Please fix this without breaking the existing range only integration behavior. The environment is offline with pandas, geopandas and the package installed.
